Deep Blue was a chess-playing machine built by IBM. In 1997 it beat the reigning world champion Garry Kasparov over six games, a result widely read as a milestone for Artificial Intelligence.

AlphaGo beat a professional Go player in 2016 using Reinforcement Learning and millions of self-played games. It was built by DeepMind, which Google had acquired two years earlier.

The Tabulating Machine Company merged with three rivals in 1911, and the combined firm was renamed IBM in 1924. IBM went on to dominate business computing for most of the twentieth century.

[S4] Synapse Multi-Hop Benchmark (chunk 27)
Claude Shannon sketched how a machine might play chess in a 1950 paper, decades before any hardware could do it, and his sketch anticipated systems like Deep Blue. He had already founded Information Theory two years earlier.

Grace Hopper championed English-like programming and drove the design of Cobol at the end of the 1950s. Cobol arrived two years after Fortran and was aimed squarely at business data processing.
